# Scheduling

[[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)]{.anchor-icon
aria-hidden="true"}](index.html#scheduling){.anchor-link
aria-labelledby="scheduling"}
:::

Scheduling is an important concept in Effect that allows you to define
recurring effectful operations. It involves the use of the
`Schedule`{dir="auto"} type, which is an immutable value that describes
a scheduled pattern for executing effects.

The `Schedule`{dir="auto"} type is structured as follows:

::: expressive-code
<figure class="frame not-content">
<pre data-language="text"><code>          ┌─── The type of output produced by the schedule          │   ┌─── The type of input consumed by the schedule          │   │     ┌─── Additional requirements for the schedule          ▼   ▼     ▼Schedule&lt;Out, In, Requirements&gt;</code></pre>
<div class="copy">
<div>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
:::

A schedule operates by consuming values of type `In`{dir="auto"} (such
as errors in the case of `retry`{dir="auto"}, or values in the case of
`repeat`{dir="auto"}) and producing values of type `Out`{dir="auto"}. It
determines when to halt or continue the execution based on input values
and its internal state.

The inclusion of a `Requirements`{dir="auto"} parameter allows the
schedule to leverage additional services or resources as needed.

Schedules are defined as a collection of intervals spread out over time.
Each interval represents a window during which the recurrence of an
effect is possible.

::: {.autolink-heading-container .level-h2 tabindex="-1"}
## Retrying and Repetition

[[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)]{.anchor-icon
aria-hidden="true"}](index.html#retrying-and-repetition){.anchor-link
aria-labelledby="retrying-and-repetition"}
:::

In the realm of scheduling, there are two related concepts:
[Retrying](../../error-management/retrying/index.html) and
[Repetition](../repetition/index.html). While they share the same
underlying idea, they differ in their focus. Retrying aims to handle
failures by executing an effect again, while repetition focuses on
executing an effect repeatedly to achieve a desired outcome.

When using schedules for retrying or repetition, each interval's
starting boundary determines when the effect will be executed again. For
example, in retrying, if an error occurs, the schedule defines when the
effect should be retried.

::: {.autolink-heading-container .level-h2 tabindex="-1"}
## Composability of Schedules

[[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)]{.anchor-icon
aria-hidden="true"}](index.html#composability-of-schedules){.anchor-link
aria-labelledby="composability-of-schedules"}
:::

Schedules are composable, meaning you can combine simple schedules to
create more complex recurrence patterns. Operators like
`Schedule.union`{dir="auto"} or `Schedule.intersect`{dir="auto"} allow
you to build sophisticated schedules by combining and modifying existing
ones. This flexibility enables you to tailor the scheduling behavior to
meet specific requirements.
